partNotes.effect_velocity_init:
Layer-1 drift at constant velocity, no bounds. Actor-def: sprite 0, flags 0, header byte $2C. The spawn bytes are decoded into $2C / $2E (see the block note), the offsets are zeroed, and after a WaitByte #01 (2 ticks) the code integrates every frame: $14 / $16 are the accumulated layer-1 X / Y offset.
Per frame (after the WaitByte, apparently without an own SetEntryHere: OQ-I051-1): $14 += $2C + effectDeltaX and forcedScrollOverride := $14 | $8000 (X); $16 += $2E + effectDeltaY and cameraDeltaY := $16 (Y); effectRenderDeltaX := the X velocity ($2C), effectRenderDeltaY := cameraDeltaY - effectScrollV. The two axes are not symmetric: X never reaches cameraDeltaX.

actors/field_reveal_object.asm.blockNote:
Gem / stat-item pickup spawned by the field-reveal events (Bank 00, 55928-56200): it drops to the floor, hops once, becomes a pullable pickup (collect_handler_gem child) and, if it is a gem, expires.

=== SPAWN ===

SpawnAfterFlags ( field_reveal_object, #$0020 ) from EnemyDefeatDispatch (every kill but the last; the child's $26 = enemies remaining, nonzero), pyCC_mystic_ball (771837) and awB1_wall_walker (769369) (child $26 = 0). The spawn copies the spawner's position and statsPtr ($7F0020).

=== WHICH PICKUP ===

- $26 nonzero, or the room's clear reward already taken (TestFlag_0300(sceneCurrent) set), or tier 0: FieldRevealFromActorStats reads the byte at +3 of the spawner's stat table. & 3 = 0 dies at once; 1 / 2 / 3 = a gem pickup with anim $04 / $05 / $06 and item $83 / $84 / $85 (1 / 2 / 5 gems, given by GiveItemToPlayer).
- Otherwise enemy_clear_reward_table[sceneCurrent] & 3 picks the room's stat item: 1 / 2 / 3 = anim $0C / $0D / $0E (the sprites of e_hp / e_str / e_def_increase) and item $80 / $81 / $82 (Max HP / STR / DEF + 1). These paths also store $FFFF in orbitAngle (no reader found: OQ-I051-4). Nothing here sets scene flag $0300 (reward_actors does for the last-kill reward): OQ-I051-5.

=== DROP AND LIFE ===

loc_00DB0B stores the item id in chatPtr ($7F000A), remembers the spawn Y in $24 and sets $26 := 7 (the step budget). With Y aligned to a 16 px row it probes the tile with BranchIfSolidHere: while the tile is solid it moves one row (16 px) down, at most 8 rows, and stops early on a tile whose collision byte is $0E; after 8 failures the target is the spawn Y + 1. The target goes to moveXAlt / moveYAlt, the actor returns to its spawn Y, flies to the target (MoveToward, 4 px per frame), hops once (Y chain $45: -2, -2, -1, -1, 0, 0, +1, +1, +2, +2), waits 12 ticks (WaitByte #0B) and spawns collect_handler_gem (SpawnAfterMarked #$2300): holding L / R then pulls the pickup toward the player.
It then animates in 100-frame blocks. A stat item (anim $0C-$0E, at least 8) repeats forever. A gem (anim $04-$06) switches to anim + 5 after the first block (the blink animations $09 / $0A / $0B, inferred: OQ-I051-7), plays 10 more frames and falls into FieldRevealDieEmpty (Die): a gem lives about 110 frames.

The old header said it checks that all enemies are cleared and stages HP / STR / DEF gem sprites. The flag means 'this room's reward is already taken', and only the tier path stages stat items; the gem path stages gems.

functions/SpawnFieldRevealEffect.asm.blockNote:
Room-reveal effect (Bank 00, 56818-57107): after the enemy that guards a hidden room part is defeated, a glowing sprite rises from the corpse, flies to the centre of the revealed region, flashes, scatters ten sparkles and swaps the background tiles (StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx + ApplyBgChange). Three actor bodies live in this file: SpawnFieldRevealEffect, field_reveal_scatter (which falls through into field_reveal_flash) and field_reveal_flash.

=== SPAWN ===

SpawnListAppend ( SpawnFieldRevealEffect, #00, #00, #$0342 ) in StandardEnemyDefeatHandler (56375), EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill (697548), pyCC_mystic_ball (771970) and awB1_wall_walker (770414). The spawner copies its deathActionIdx ($7F0024, the event-block index of its scene record) into the child; EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill guards the spawn with event flag $0100 + index so each reveal fires once.

=== TARGET ===

event_block_table is indexed by deathActionIdx x 8. The bytes used are +3 width, +4 height, +5 dstX and +6 dstY (event-block-def, tile units). The flight target is the centre of the destination rectangle in pixels: moveXAlt = (2 x dstX + width) x 8, moveYAlt = (2 x dstY + height) x 8. orbitAngle := width / 2 and orbitDiameter := height / 2 are passed to the scatter particles as their range tier.

=== SEQUENCE ===

Flags $0342, palette 0, anim $29: three rising passes (Y chains $02, $12, $14), a two-pass hover loop, sprite priority $30, then StageMove to the target at 4 px per frame (TickMove). On arrival: a field_reveal_flash child, a 2-tick wait (WaitByte #01), $10 |= $2000, then ten field_reveal_scatter children (one every 5 ticks: WaitByte #03 is 4 ticks and LoopEnd yields once more; each gets the half-width and half-height), then StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx (SFX $0F on both channels, stages the swap), ApplyBgChange and Die. Each child gets $12 |= $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier, which CopyActorState clears).

The old header named an 'Incan Ruins wind trap' as a user (the four callers above are the real ones) and called +3 / +5 the 'target X tile' and 'X size'; they are the width and dstX.

functions/game_over_sequence.asm.blockNote:
Player death sequence (Bank 00, 54831-55263) with its helper actors. combat_collision.CheckPlayerDeath sets playerFlags $0200 when playerHp is zero, replaces the player actor's entry point with GameOverSequence and calls StopPlayerOnDeath, so the player actor itself runs this script from the next tick. Entry points: GameOverSequence (player), GameOverCutsceneSprites (spawned by it), GameOverSparkleDriftA/B (spawned by that) and DeathWakeupMessage (spawned by player_character after the respawn).

=== TIMELINE ===

Frame 0: player $10 |= $0040 (dead; shadow_shimmer reads it) and joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC (every button and the D-pad, Start and Select included).
After 33 ticks (WaitByte #20): spawn DeathPaletteFadeThinker (palette bundles $10, then $0E) and GameOverCutsceneSprites (the sparkles).
After 120 more ticks (WaitByte #77): clear player $10 bit $8000 (the player stops using DecomposePlayerSprites), SFX $0C on both channels (the same SFX as the Dark Space warp) and play animation #1C of spriteset_enemies once (also used by the Dark Space warp).
Fade: orbitAngle starts at 15; every pass writes counter - 1 to INIDISP (brightness 14 down to 0) and waits 4 ticks (WaitByte #03), 60 ticks in all. Forced blank is never set.
Then two one-frame palette thinkers (PaletteResetAndKillThinker with bundle IDs $0B and $0D: sub-entry 0 of each bundle is applied once), one yield and the respawn choice.

=== RESPAWN CHOICE ===

gemCount >= 100 (revive): gemCount -= 100, playerHp = playerMaxHp >> 1, and the respawn record is the one stored by the last warp the player took (reviveWarpPtr / reviveWarpBank, $0AF4 / $0AF6; ExecuteWarp writes a pointer to entry + 4 for every warp). Form and wramFlags are kept.
gemCount < 100 (real game over): gemCount = 0, characterForm = 0 (Will), or 2 (Shadow) when sceneCurrent is $E8 (the Dark Gaia arena in the comet lair; presumably because that fight is played as Shadow), playerHp = playerMaxHp, the 16 words of wramFlags ($0A80-$0A9F: dungeon kill and puzzle flags) are cleared, and the respawn record is sceneSaveData / sceneSaveDataBank ($0AF0 / $0AF2), which ExecuteWarp writes only for warps whose entry byte 9 has bit 7 set.

=== SHARED RESPAWN TAIL ===

Reads the warp record at DBR:Y: byte 0 = scene (sceneNext, 8-bit store), +1 and +3 = spawn X and Y (warpDestX / warpDestY), +5 = facing with bit 7 masked (warpFacing), +6 = packed camera window (warpScrollParams). Then gfxCacheIdxB := $0404, gameOverWakeupFlag += 1, worldReadyFlag := 0 (ExecuteSceneTransition then skips the exit transition, because the screen is already black, and runs the enter transition) and SetEntryHere + RTL; the scene change takes over.

=== WAKE-UP MESSAGE ===

player_character spawns DeathWakeupMessage (SpawnAfterFlags $2000) at the start of the next scene when gameOverWakeupFlag ($0AF8) is set. It masks the joypad with $CFFC (Select and Start stay live), clears the flag, waits 3 ticks (WaitByte #02), prints one of three strings chosen by characterForm (0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow), unmasks and dies. The message follows a revive as well as a real game over. After a real game over the form is Will (Shadow in $E8), so the Freedan line appears only after a revive as Freedan.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

The ROM masks the joypad with $FFF0 (and $CFF0 in DeathWakeupMessage); db-us/transforms.json (block game_over_sequence) widens both to $FFFC / $CFFC so the software-only buttons $0004 and $0008 are masked too, and the extracted asm shows the transformed values. The old comment credited the first block with spawning both helpers (it is a 33-tick wait first); 'sound #$0C' is the 16-bit pair $0C0C on both channels. The old header did not say that 100 gems are paid in the revive case, that the wramFlags are cleared only on a real game over, or that two different warp records are used.

system/dark_space/sE6_gaia.asm.blockNote:
Dark Space / Gaia hub (scene $E6, the room reached from the Dark Space portals and from the diary menu's load) plus a shared character-transformation library (Bank 08, 579499-587528; GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle in Bank 09, 630928-630997). The same spawn list is also used by scene $09, which has no scene-meta entry. scene_meta_00E6 loads spm_darkspace_sprites ($0579 bytes) and plays track $16 (bgm_space_beyond_time).

=== STRUCTURE ===

DarkSpaceMainInit spawns three children with SpawnAfter: FireflySpawnerLoop, GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle. SpawnAfter inserts each new actor right after the parent, so the main actor's $06 link ends up on the LAST one spawned, the voice sparkle (the old notes called it the Gaia NPC link). Every 'LDY $06 / STA $0024, Y' below is therefore the voice sparkle's on / off switch ($FFFF = on, 0 = off), not an NPC interaction lock.
It then validates globalScriptIndex ($0AAC: the room variant, written by the portal actor or restored by the diary load; 4 or more becomes 0), keeps it in $0AB2 (saved with the game, restored by the diary menu), clears $0AAC and switch-cases to a layout: 0 DS_LayoutBasic (Gaia only), 1 DS_LayoutTransform (statues chosen by characterForm), 2 DS_LayoutAbility (ability orb chosen by the scene), 3 DS_LayoutSpecial (sets $0AAC = 1 and runs layout 1; this is the pyramid's Dark Space, where GaiaHint_AuraItem tests $0AAC and gives the Aura item).
Every room polls BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles zones (x1, y1, x2, y2 in tiles): Gaia (7,8)-(9,9) = GaiaDialogueEntry, left statue (3,A)-(5,B), right statue (B,A)-(D,B), exit (5,D)-(B,F) = DarkSpaceExit. Each room has a wait state (the player is still standing in a zone: nothing happens, so a dialogue cannot retrigger) and an active state that dispatches the zones; the *Wait / *TileWait pairs and the loc_ labels after them are these two states.
The called scripts (GaiaDialogueEntry, the *TransformDialogue routines) are entered with CallNear and end with RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to the room loop.

=== EXIT ===

DarkSpaceExit masks the joypad, hides the player ($10 |= $2000), puts this actor on him, plays SFX $0C on both channels and the dissolve animation $1C of spriteset_enemies once, waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), then fills the warp words: sceneNext = $0B12 (the scene the player warped from, saved by ExecuteWarp), player spawn X = $0B08 x 16 and Y = ($0B0C + 2) x 16 (the source warp rectangle's tile position), facing 3 and the packed camera window $0B10 / $0B11 -> warpScrollParams. gfxCacheIdxB = $0101 is the transition speed (exit and enter 1), gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 is exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade. The old notes called the destination a camera position and $0101 a brightness fade.

=== GAIA DIALOGUE ===

GaiaDialogueEntry: 6-tick pause (WaitByte #05), voice sparkle on, first visit (event flag $DC) the intro text, then GaiaHealAndHints. If HP < max it prints the 'hurt' text and writes hpToHeal = 40; UpdateHUD turns that request into +1 HP every 8 frames (SFX $0D) until HP = max (the loop yields until then). The hint is chosen by the position of the source scene in GaiaHintSceneTable (34 scenes, one GaiaHint_xx handler each; 21 of them have no text and go straight to the save prompt). GaiaSavePrompt: 'Record what's happened so far?' (DialogueOptions: entry 0 = cancel, 1 = first option, 2 = second option). Record = SaveGameState_Scene for the active slot ($0D8C), SFX $29, 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then 'Continue your journey?': Yes (entry 1) = GaiaDontRecord, 'Then go.', returns to the room; No (entry 2) = GaiaContinueJourney, 'Then rest a while.', fades to track $0E (bgm_longing_for_the_past) and the actor yields forever. The two labels are named after the first prompt and are swapped for the second one.

=== FORMS AND ABILITIES ===

characterForm ($0AD4): 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow. A statue dialogue writes a Transform_* routine into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000 / $0002, $0008 = 0) and sets playerFlags $0800; the player then plays it (player body entry #05, the transformation frames), the routine sets characterForm and DarkSpaceRestoreControl clears $0800 and sends the player back to PlayerIdleEntry. The Shadow statue needs event flag $B4, whose only writer is daC8_neil (the Neil reunion in the Dao dormitory; the old header said it is unlocked at Ankor Wat); first Freedan visit flag $F7, first Shadow visit flag $DD.
The Transform_* routines are a shared library: Transform_WillToShadow is entered from sE5_epilogue, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and btE4_kara; Transform_ShadowToWill from pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and pyCD_jackal; Transform_FreedanToWill from sg55_mystic_statue, ir29_transform, ir1C_lily, ec13_lily, pyCD_jackal and mu67_bomb (13 files in all).
AbilitySceneTable has 6 entries of (scene, abilityBitmask bit): $15 Psycho Dash $01, $62 Psycho Slider $02, $86 Spin Dash $04, $42 Dark Friar $10, $A7 Aura Barrier $20, $B8 Earthquaker $40, ended by $00. The low nibble holds the Will abilities, the high nibble the Freedan abilities; the old header called byte 1 'ability index + statue type'. The table position is the ability index used by table_08EB8F (names) and table_08EBD3 (descriptions) through globalScriptIndex. DS_LayoutAbility shows the orb for the current scene (BG change $86 and orb at (64,109) for a Will ability, $8B and (64,84) for a Freedan ability); AbilityOrbActor dies when the bit is already in abilityBitmask, otherwise waits for the player at the statue zone, turns him into the form that can use it (Will for the low nibble, Freedan for the high nibble) with LookupStatueType, ORs the bit in, plays the orb flight, fanfare (track $18) and the two texts.

=== SPRITES (spm_darkspace_sprites) ===

Animation #00 (4 frames, hold $63 then $0C x 3) is GaiaNpcSprite; #01 to #03 are the three sparkle variants of GaiaVoiceSparkle; #0A (32 frames of hold 0, a 16 x 16 spark alternating with an 8 x 8 tile) is the ability orb. #04 to #09 (8 x 8 effect tiles) are not used by this file. FireflyParticle and DarkSpaceExit use spriteset_enemies.

=== NOT REFERENCED ===

No reference was found in extracted/ for: DS_AuraItemRoom and its handlers, AuraItemInteraction and its helpers (with dialogstring_08EFEF / 08F003 / 08F060), DarkSpaceAmbientParticle, the code at loc_08DA6B / loc_08DA77 (after an unconditional BRA), and the unused hint strings dialogstring_08DEC6, 08E066, 08E0C7, 08E109, 08E19C, 08E261, 08E2B9 and 08E615.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

Replaced claims: byte 1 of AbilitySceneTable is an ability bit, not an index with a statue nibble; the continue prompt's Yes / No were described the other way round; $06 is the voice sparkle, not the Gaia NPC, and $24 is its voice switch; 'Unmask D-pad and face buttons' ($0F00) is the D-pad only; hpToHeal 40 is a heal request (not 'damage flash ticks'); warpDestX / warpDestY and the $0B08-$0B12 values are the player's spawn position and source scene, not a camera; GaiaNpcSprite loops an idle animation (it is not a single frame); the Shadow flag $B4 is set by Neil, not at Ankor Wat; 'spriteset #05 (transformation frames)' is player body entry #05 and the 'transformation spriteset' of the exit effect is spriteset_enemies; Transform_ShadowToFreedan uses SetEntryHereAndYield, not SetEntryExit.

system/title_screen/sFC_title_start_hand.blockNote:
Title / prologue Start handler (Bank 0B, 772529-772609): waits for Start, then sends the game to the diary menu (scene $FA).

Two actor-defs share one poll loop. sFC_title_start_handler is spawned with sFC_title_intro by scene_event_0CE56D (the title scene $FC list) and first waits WaitWord $021B = 540 ticks (~9 s) so the intro's opening seconds cannot be skipped. sFC_actor_0BC9BD polls at once; it is spawned in the actor lists of the four prologue scenes ($8C-$8F, next to pr8C_prologue1/5, pr8D_prologue2, pr8E_prologue3 and pr8F_prologue4), so Start skips the prologue slides as well.

Both variants first mask nearly every button out of joypadCurrent (joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC; vanilla $FFF0, widened by transforms.json) and then poll with COP BranchIfPressed #$1001. In that mask word bit 0 is not a button: it makes the handler test joypadRaw instead of joypadCurrent (see docs/cop/families/input.md, BranchIfPressed), which is how Start ($1000) still gets through the mask. R is not tested.

On Start, TitleToDiaryTransition sets transitionBrightness = 0 and the transition parameters (gfxCacheIdxB = 0: speed 0; gfxCacheIdxA = 1: exit type 1 = instant blank, enter type 0 = graduated fade), queues scene $FA at ($0100,$0370) with COP QueueMapChange, yields one frame, runs one VBlankWaitAndJoypad with DP forced to $0000, and then holds INIDISP = $00 (force blank) every frame until the scene change replaces the actor.

partNotes.ArrivalAndTravelSetup: Child actor (flags $3800, script-driven). Phases: 44-tick zoom-out ($B8 falls), for a menu trip a 16-tick wait + HdmaWindowEffect + wait for the player's route, the 93-tick tilt phase with the start name ($B6 grows), then the companion dots. It finally becomes the leader's dot through the shared loop in CompanionDotMovement and dies when the route ends.
partNotes.RouteEndHandler: Route byte $FF. A pending subroutine return (nonzero $0D5C) continues the caller. A true end: clear route and choice ids (the dots notice and die), show the destination name (scene $0D6E) for 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then lower $B6 by $10 per frame until it would go negative (the map is flat again; Start skips to the scene change). Landing: $B6 := 0, transition speeds gfxCacheIdxB := $0406, restore the deferred scene change, clear the state block, and from then on add the TickGravity delta to $B8 every frame (zoom-in dive) until the scene changes.

system/world_map/WorldMapController.asm.blockNote:
World map controller (scene $FE actor, Bank 03, 238321-239290). The scene is a Mode 7 map; this file runs the arrival zoom, the destination menu, the companion dots, the route playback and the dive into the destination scene.

=== HOW A TRIP STARTS ===

Both kinds of trip arrive through CheckSceneTransition / ExecuteSceneTransition, which see a nonzero $0D52/$0D53 and then move $0D52 -> $0D54 (worldMapPlayerX), $0652 -> $0D6C, sceneNext -> $0D6E and sceneCurrent -> $0D6F, and switch to scene $FE:
- Menu trip: the exit actor in a town or dungeon entrance (overworld_exit) writes $0D60 := 0 and runs COP StageWorldMapChoice (start X, start Y, choice id). The choice id in $0D58 selects a menu in world_map_options.
- Scripted trip: an NPC departure script (13 of them, e.g. ec0A_kara, wa79_neil, daC8_neil) fills the party array, runs COP StageWorldMapMove (start X, start Y, 0, route id) and has already queued the destination with QueueMapChange. StageWorldMapMove clears $0D58, so there is no menu.

=== STATE BLOCK $0D52-$0D6F ===

| Address | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| $0D52 | staged start X; nonzero = a world-map entry is pending (moved to $0D54 and cleared on arrival) |
| $0D54 / $0D56 | worldMapPlayerX / Y: start position on the 1024 x 1024 map |
| $0D58 | choice id (0 = none). The low 5 bits index world_map_options |
| $0D5A | route id (0 = none). Index into world_map_routes, set by COP #65 / #67 |
| $0D5C | route subroutine return pointer (0 = none) |
| $0D5E | written by COP #65 / #67 (always 0), never read |
| $0D60-$0D6A | party array: six words of spm_overworld_sprites animation indices. $0D60 is the leader, $0D62-$0D6A are up to five companions, 0 = empty |
| $0D6C | deferred $0652 (scroll parameters of the queued scene change) |
| $0D6E | destination scene (low byte); a scripted trip gets it from ExecuteSceneTransition, a menu trip from DeferSceneTransition |
| $0D6F | scene being left (the start name is looked up with it) |

ClearWorldMapState zeroes $0D52-$0D6D (14 words, CPY #$001C), so $0D6E/$0D6F survive the trip.

=== MODE 7 PARAMETERS THE CONTROLLER DRIVES ===

Mode7PerspectiveInit (scene thinker, see mode7_perspective) sets the global words $B8 := $0400, $B6 := 0, $BC := 0 and the centre $CA/$CC := ($0D54, $0D56). Per frame it turns them into the M7A-M7D HDMA tables:
- $B8 is the divisor at the top scanline: smaller = zoomed out, larger = zoomed in ($80 is about 1:1).
- $B6 is how much the divisor grows per scanline: 0 = flat map, larger = stronger perspective.
- $BC is the rotation index (512 steps per turn). Route steps change it, so the map turns during a trip. The old comments called it elevation.
- $CA/$CC are the world X/Y (map centre). cameraTargetX/Y follow as centre - ($80, $70).

=== TIMELINE ===

1. WorldMapController (code_03A2F4): characterForm := 0, two palette-reset thinkers (bundle $0B: Will's normal sprite colours, CGRAM $81-$8F), ClearAllWramFlags, mask the buttons, spawn ArrivalAndTravelSetup as a child (flags $3800). With no choice id it dies here; otherwise it gives the child animScratch2 |= $0804, saves DeferSceneTransition with SetSavedPtr and runs world_map_options[choice & $1F] (menu and handler).
2. ArrivalAndTravelSetup, 44 ticks: places itself (the leader's dot) at the start position, centres the camera, then each tick adds the TickGravity delta (always negative: -$20 rising to about -2) to $B8. The divisor falls from $0400 to about $34 (hand-computed), a zoom-out from 8x in to a wide view.
3. Menu trips only: wait 16 ticks (WaitByte #0F), spawn HdmaWindowEffect, then poll $0D5A every frame (RTL = try again next frame) while the menu is open. Choosing Quit leaves it at 0: the handler has already queued the scene you came from and DeferSceneTransition just dies, so this actor idles until the scene changes.
4. Tilt phase (loc_03A3A4), 93 ticks: shows the start-area name (see world_map_names), adds the TickGravity delta ((t * (t >> 1)) >> 7, growing) to $B6 and 1 to $B8. $B6 ends at about $03F0, so the flat map tilts into a strong perspective view. Then the name is cleared ($00DA := 0).
5. Companion dots: the party array is scanned from $0D62, N companions pick entry N of companion_position_tables, and one CompanionDotMovement actor per companion is spawned. RouteAnimationEngine is spawned and this actor becomes the leader's dot.
6. RouteAnimationEngine plays the route bytes (see world_map_routes): X, Y and rotation steps change $CA/$CC/$BC.
7. RouteEndHandler: dots die, the destination name shows for 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), $B6 falls by $10 per frame until the map is flat again (Start skips everything), then the deferred sceneNext/$0652 are restored and the controller dives: $B8 grows by an increasing delta, a zoom-in while the scene exit transition runs.

=== SPRITES (spm_overworld_sprites.sprite.asm, not annotatable with the merge tool) ===

The spritemap (scene_meta_00FE, $1238 bytes, gfx_overworld_actors, palette pal_overworld_sprites at colour $90) has 14 animations. The leader and companion dots use the animation index from the party array as actor field $28.
- 0-5: 4-frame cycles (hold 7), one per party slot value (art identity not checked). 6: three 1-part frames.
- 7-A: four 5-frame sets. wa79_neil fills the party array with 7, 8, 9, A for the Watermia to Euro leg (menu handlers set only $0D60 := 7), so these look like the pieces of one vehicle (not checked at runtime).
- B: 3 frames of 24-28 parts, used as the leader by daC8_neil (Dao to Over Babel). C: same shape, no writer found. D: 4 frames, used as the leader by wa78_men (Watermia to South Cape).

=== KEY ROUTINES ===

- DeferSceneTransition: callback after the menu handler; keeps the queued scene out of the way while the route plays.
- ArrivalAndTravelSetup: arrival zoom, menu wait, tilt phase, dot formation, route launch; then runs as the leader's dot.
- CompanionDotMovement: one companion dot (also the shared dot loop).
- RouteAnimationEngine: interpreter for the world_map_routes bytes. RouteEndHandler: end-of-route name, untilt and dive.
- LookupMapName: scene id -> name string pointer.
